name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Dan Meuser running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
No public polling or expert ratings; markets price Meuser at 96%
model.rationale: The R+19 lean, Meuser's incumbency and his roughly three-to-one fundraising advantage over Rachel Wallace all point to a safe Republican hold, and Polymarket prices his win at 96%. With no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise, the forecast stays near the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Meuser underperforming his lean, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dan Meuser seeks another term in a northeastern Pennsylvania district that leans about nineteen points Republican, making this one of the safer Republican seats on the ballot. Meuser has raised about $1.9 million and holds a cash advantage over Democrat Rachel Wallace, who has raised roughly $700,000. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency and money. Prediction markets give Meuser about a 96% chance of winning. A Democratic upset would require a dramatic, district-wide shift well beyond anything visible in the current evidence.
